claim_being_audited: The Actor claims the model can be certified for release on the current record, based on aggregate readiness and general risk-management/model-card guidance, while treating the small-business onboarding gap as a monitored residual limitation.

concern_ledger.concern: Materiality appears triggered because the affected small-business onboarding segment is named in two paid pilot commitments.
concern_ledger.evidence_needed_to_close: Admissible evidence showing the segment is not a contractual customer segment or named launch use case under policy, or evidence that the requirement was satisfied another way.
concern_ledger.why_it_blocks_compliance: If the weakness is material, policy requires disclosure, resolution, or approved risk acceptance before launch; current certification cannot be found compliant without one of those links.

concern_ledger.concern: No admissible evidence shows the limitation was disclosed before launch.
concern_ledger.evidence_needed_to_close: A dated admissible launch artifact or model card showing disclosure of the small-business onboarding gap.
concern_ledger.why_it_blocks_compliance: Policy expressly requires disclosure of material limitations for named launch use cases unless resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance.

concern_ledger.concern: No admissible evidence shows approved risk acceptance for the unresolved gap.
concern_ledger.evidence_needed_to_close: An admissible approval record granting risk acceptance for this specific limitation before launch.
concern_ledger.why_it_blocks_compliance: Absent resolution or disclosure, approved risk acceptance is the remaining policy path; without it, certification lacks required support.

concern_ledger.concern: Legal review is still open on whether the gap must be disclosed.
concern_ledger.evidence_needed_to_close: A final legal determination or equivalent admissible resolution of the disclosure question.
concern_ledger.why_it_blocks_compliance: Pending legal review leaves a required compliance predicate unresolved and prevents treating the issue as closed.

decision_criteria: Use 'compliant' only if admissible evidence satisfies the policy threshold.
A weakness is material if it affects a contractual customer segment, protected segment, or named launch use case.
Product labels such as non-core or low-volume do not resolve materiality when the affected segment is named in customer commitments or when legal review is pending.
Material limitations for named launch use cases must be disclosed unless resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch.
Aggregate readiness and absence of severity-one incidents are relevant but not sufficient to override a specific unmet disclosure/risk-acceptance requirement.
evidence_requests: Provide admissible evidence that the small-business onboarding limitation was disclosed in the model card or other required launch materials before certification.
Provide an approved risk acceptance covering this specific gap for the named segment before launch.
Provide a final legal determination on whether disclosure is required for the named small-business onboarding segment.
Provide admissible evidence that the paid pilot commitments do not constitute a contractual customer segment or named launch use case under policy, if that is the position.
specific_concerns: The admissible record shows a known weakness in a segment named in two paid pilot commitments, which makes the issue material under the stated policy standard.
There is no admissible evidence that the gap has been resolved, disclosed, or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch.
Legal review on required disclosure is still open, so a required policy predicate remains unresolved.
General NIST-style monitoring principles and model-card content guidance do not substitute for the policy-required showing for this specific launch decision.

The Actor's justification overrelies on aggregate readiness and non-severity-one rehearsal results, which do not cure a material undisclosed limitation in a named launch use case or contractual segment.
unsupported_claims: That the remaining issue can be treated as a monitored limitation within the model-card and post-launch process without evidence of actual pre-launch disclosure or approved risk acceptance.
That certification is presently defensible under policy on the current record.
Any implicit claim that product's 'non-core' characterization resolves materiality despite named paid pilot commitments and pending legal review.
